questions.question: Which of the following quantities remains unchanged when a charged particle moves in a magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kinetic energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **charged particle** moves in a magnetic field, the force acting on it is always **perpendicular** to its velocity.
 
• Since the magnetic force does no work (due to being perpendicular to displacement), there is no change in the **magnitude of the velocity**, and hence the **kinetic energy** remains constant.
 
• The motion of the particle in the magnetic field results in a **circular or helical trajectory**, depending on the initial velocity and angle with the field.
 
• The magnetic field causes the particle to change its **direction** continuously, but not its **speed**.
 
• This principle is used in many applications, such as **cyclotrons** and other particle accelerators, where particles are made to move in circular paths without changing their energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Direction of velocity**__

 __
 
• The **direction of velocity** of the charged particle changes continuously because of the perpendicular force exerted by the magnetic field.
 
• This change in direction results in a **circular or helical motion**, depending on the initial conditions.
 
 
 
• **Momentum direction**__
 __
 
• The **momentum direction** also changes continuously because the velocity direction is changing due to the magnetic force.
 
• However, the **magnitude of momentum** remains constant as the speed is unchanged.
 
 
 
• **Angular momentum**__
 
 
• The **angular momentum** of the particle about the center of its circular trajectory changes due to the magnetic force acting as the centripetal force.
 
• This leads to periodic motion, as seen in devices like **mass spectrometers**.

questions.question: Which of the following factors best explains the formation of ox-bow lakes along river courses?

options.text: Sudden uplift of riverbeds by tectonic activity
Lateral erosion on the outer banks and deposition on the inner banks

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Lateral erosion on the outer banks and deposition on the inner banks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ox-bow lakes** are formed due to the **meandering nature of rivers**, which is a natural process in the middle and lower courses of rivers.
 
• **Lateral erosion** occurs on the **outer banks** of a river bend, where the velocity of water is higher, causing the banks to erode and the bend to become more pronounced over time.
 
• At the same time, **deposition** happens on the **inner banks** of the bend, where the water velocity is lower, leading to the accumulation of sediments.
 
• This process eventually creates an extreme curve in the river, and when the neck of the meander becomes very narrow, the river may cut through it during a flood or high flow event, forming a new, straighter channel.
 
• The abandoned meander loop, isolated from the main river, forms an **ox-bow lake**.
 
• Ox-bow lakes are characteristic features of **low-lying floodplains** where rivers flow gently.
 
• This process is a combination of **fluvial erosion and deposition**, driven by the natural dynamics of the flowing water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• **Tectonic activity** can alter river courses, but it does not typically result in the formation of **ox-bow lakes**.
 
• Sudden uplift may lead to the formation of features like **waterfalls** or **gorges**, but not ox-bow lakes.
 
 
 
• **Tectonic uplift disrupting the flow**__
 __
 
• **Tectonic uplift** can modify river systems by creating ** or altering gradients, but this process is not related to the creation of ox-bow lakes**.
 
 
 
• **Glacial retreat leaving depressions**__
 
 
• **Glacial retreat** can lead to the formation of features like **kettle lakes** and **moraines**, which are different from ox-bow lakes formed in fluvial systems.
 
• This process is associated with glacial landscapes rather than river meandering.

questions.question: The Contact Process is used for the manufacturing of which of the following chemicals?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sulphuric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Contact Process** is an industrial method used for the manufacturing of **sulphuric acid**, one of the most widely used chemicals in the world.
 
• It involves the catalytic oxidation of **sulphur dioxide (SO₂)** to **sulphur trioxide (SO₃)** using a **vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅)** catalyst.
 
• The process consists of three main steps:
 
 
• Production of **sulphur dioxide** by burning sulphur or roasting sulphide ores.
 
• Conversion of sulphur dioxide to **sulphur trioxide** in the presence of a catalyst.
 
• Absorption of sulphur trioxide in **concentrated sulphuric acid** to form oleum, which is then diluted to produce sulphuric acid.
 
 
 
• **Sulphuric acid** is a highly versatile chemical used in various industries, including the manufacture of fertilizers, chemicals, petroleum refining, and wastewater treatment.
 
• The Contact Process is preferred over older methods such as the **Lead Chamber Process** due to its higher efficiency and production of purer sulphuric acid.
 
• The chemical equation for the key step in the process is: **2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃** (in the presence of a catalyst).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ammonia**__

 __
 
• **Ammonia** is manufactured using the **Haber Process**, not the Contact Process.
 
• It is a key ingredient in the production of **fertilizers** such as urea and ammonium nitrate.
 
• The Haber Process involves the reaction of **nitrogen (N₂)** and **hydrogen (H₂)** gases under high pressure and temperature, using an iron catalyst.
 
 
 
• **Nitric acid**__
 __
 
• **Nitric acid** is manufactured using the **Ostwald Process**, not the Contact Process.
 
• The Ostwald Process involves the oxidation of **ammonia** to produce nitric acid.
 
• Nitric acid is widely used in the production of **explosives, fertilizers**, and other chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Hydrochloric acid**__
 
 
• **Hydrochloric acid** is typically produced as a byproduct of industrial processes, such as the manufacture of **chlorine** or **polyvinyl chloride (PVC)**.
 
• It is used in a variety of applications, including **metal cleaning, pH control, and production of organic compounds**.

questions.question: What does the shortcut key Ctrl + S do in most software applications?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

⇒ 6 × 60 = Q₂ × 120

**∴ The correct answer is 3 rubber-bands.**

Selling 6 rubber-bands for Re. 1 results in a loss of 40%.

•

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of 6 rubber-bands be x.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of 6 rubber-bands = Re. 1

⇒ Loss = 40%

⇒ CP × (100 − 40) / 100 = SP

⇒ x × 60 / 100 = 1

questions.question: The product of two consecutive natural numbers is 210. The greater of the two numbers is:

The product of two consecutive natural numbers n × (n + 1) is slightly greater than n².

Find a perfect square closest to 210 to approximate the numbers.

We know that 14² = 196 and 15² = 225.

Since 196 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The product of two consecutive natural numbers is 210.

**Calculation:**

Let the two consecutive natural numbers be x and (x + 1).

⇒ x² + x = 210

⇒ x² + x − 210 = 0

⇒ x² + 15x − 14x − 210 = 0

⇒ x(x + 15) − 14(x + 15) = 0

⇒ (x − 14)(x + 15) = 0

⇒ x = 14

Natural numbers are the set of positive integers starting from 1 (1, 2, 3, 4, ...). They do not include zero, fractions, or negative numbers.

Consecutive Numbers

Consecutive numbers are numbers that follow each other continuously from smallest to largest with a constant difference of 1 (e.g., n, n+1, n+2).

Quadratic Equation Roots

A quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has two roots. If the constant term is negative while a is positive, the roots will have opposite signs.

questions.question: The LCM of the numbers 2.7 and 0.096 is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert decimals to their simplest fractional forms: 2.7 = 27/10 and 0.096 = 96/1000 = 12/125.

LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators.

⇒ LCM(27, 12) = 108

⇒ HCF(10, 125) = 5

⇒ Result = 108 ÷ 5 = 21.6

**∴ The correct answer is 21.6.**

Numbers: 2.7 and 0.096

Convert decimals to integers by multiplying by a power of 10, find their LCM, and divide the result by the same power of 10.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The maximum number of decimal places is 3 (in 0.096). So, multiply both numbers by 1000 to convert them to integers.

⇒ 2.7 × 1000 = 2700

⇒ 0.096 × 1000 = 96

⇒ Prime factorization of 2700 = 2² × 3³ × 5²

⇒ Prime factorization of 96 = 2⁵ × 3¹

⇒ LCM(2700, 96) = 2⁵ × 3³ × 5²

⇒ LCM(2700, 96) = 32 × 27 × 25 = 21600

⇒ To find the LCM of the original decimal numbers, divide the result by 1000:

⇒ LCM = 21600 ÷ 1000 = 21.6

**∴ The correct answer is 21.6.**

Fractions must be reduced to their simplest form first. LCM = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators).

HCF of Fractions

Fractions must be reduced to their simplest form first. HCF = (HCF of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators).

LCM of Decimals

Convert decimals into integers by multiplying them with the highest power of 10 present in any decimal, find the LCM, and then divide the result by the same power of 10.

Product of Two Numbers

For any two numbers a and b: LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b.

Law of Quotient: am ÷ aⁿ = am − ⁿ

Law of Product: am × aⁿ = am ⁺ ⁿ

According to the BODMAS rule, division and multiplication have the same precedence, so we evaluate the expression from left to right.

⇒ (83−⁶ ÷ 83¹⁶) × 83−⁸

Applying the Law of Quotient for the first part:

⇒ 83−⁶ − ¹⁶ × 83−⁸

⇒ 83−²² × 83−⁸

When a power is raised to another power, you multiply the exponents: (am)ⁿ = am × ⁿ

A negative exponent denotes the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive exponent: a−ⁿ = 1 ÷ aⁿ

questions.question: The number of prime numbers lying between 303 and 311, both included, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Numbers from 303 to 311: 303, 304, 305, 306, 307, 308, 309, 310, 311.

Eliminate even numbers and numbers ending in 5: 303, 307, 309, 311.

Check divisibility by 3 (sum of digits): 303 (sum 6) and 309 (sum 12) are multiples of 3.

Remaining numbers are 307 and 311, which are not divisible by primes up to √311 (7, 11, 13, 17).

Thus, 307 and 311 are the only prime numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Range of numbers: 303 to 311 (both included)

**Concept Used:**

A prime number has only two distinct divisors: 1 and itself.

To check if a number N is prime, we divide it by all prime numbers ≤ √N.

**Calculations:**

⇒ List of numbers to check: 303, 304, 305, 306, 307, 308, 309, 310, 311.

⇒ Even numbers (304, 306, 308, 310) are divisible by 2.

⇒ Number ending in 5 (305) is divisible by 5.

⇒ Remaining odd numbers: 303, 307, 309, 311.

⇒ Checking divisibility by 3 (sum of digits must be a multiple of 3):

⇒ 303 → 3 + 0 + 3 = 6 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ 309 → 3 + 0 + 9 = 12 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ Remaining numbers to check for primality: 307 and 311.

⇒ Approximate square root of 311 ≈ 17.6.

⇒ Prime numbers ≤ 17 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17.

⇒ Checking 307: Not divisible by 7, 11, 13, 17. Hence, 307 is a prime number.

⇒ Checking 311: Not divisible by 7, 11, 13, 17. Hence, 311 is a prime number.

⇒ Total count of prime numbers = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that cannot be formed by multiplying two smaller natural numbers. It has exactly two divisors: 1 and itself.

Primality Test

To check if a given number N is prime, find the approximate square root of N. Divide N by all prime numbers less than or equal to √N. If N is not divisible by any of these primes, it is a prime number.

Co-Prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime (or mutually prime) if the only positive integer that divides both of them is 1. Their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is always 1.

Composite Numbers

Numbers that have more than two factors are called composite numbers. The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.
</p

**(II) All conditioners are detergents:**

The statements do not provide enough information to guarantee this is true.

So, **Only conclusion (I) follows.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
